facts.statement: Pachydyptes is known from a few bones found in Late Eocene rocks in the Otago region.
facts.quote: This taxon is known from a few bones from Late Eocene (37 to 34 MYA) rocks in the area of Otago

facts.statement: The fossils were found in two clades located near the base of a tree.
facts.quote: found in two clades near a base of a tree

facts.statement: Pachydyptes lived during the Late Eocene, between 37 and 34 million years ago.
facts.quote: Late Eocene (37 to 34 MYA)

facts.statement: G.G. Simpson estimated that Pachydyptes stood 140 to 160 cm tall and weighed between 80 and possibly over 100 kg.
facts.quote: G.G. Simpson, an evolutionary biologist, estimated a height of 140 to 160 cm (about 5 ft) and a weight of around 80 to possibly over 100 kg

facts.statement: Pachydyptes was the second-tallest penguin ever known, surpassed only by Anthropornis nordenskjoeldi in height.
facts.quote: It was the second-tallest penguin ever, surpassed only by Anthropornis nordenskjoeldi in height

facts.statement: Pachydyptes was slightly larger than Icadyptes salasi, which is the best-identified of the giant penguins.
facts.quote: Pachydyptes was slightly larger than Icadyptes salasi, the best-identified of the giant penguins.

facts.statement: Pachydyptes is classified as a genus.
facts.quote: genus: Pachydyptes

facts.statement: The species of the genus Pachydyptes is Pachydyptes ponderosus.
facts.quote: species: ponderosus

facts.statement: The genus Pachydyptes was described by Oliver in 1930.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Oliver, 1930

facts.statement: Pachydyptes belongs to the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Palaeeudyptinae

facts.statement: Pachydyptes is a member of the family Spheniscidae.

facts.statement: Pachydyptes belongs to the class Aves.

facts.statement: Pachydyptes belongs to the kingdom Animalia.

facts.quote: Time range: Priabonian to Priabonian (37.71 to 33.9 million years ago)
